newsitem.title: USA: US Energy Sec discusses successor with Clinton.
newsitem.headline: US Energy Sec discusses successor with Clinton.

text.p: U.S. Energy Secretary Hazel O'Leary said Tuesday she has talked with President Clinton about choosing her replacement, and said the next energy secretary will not be named in the first batch of cabinet selections.

"I talked to the President and I would expect to have continuing dialogue with the principals in the White House..." O'Leary told reporters after attending a meeting of the Secretary of Energy Advisory Board.
Asked about when her replacement would be named, O'Leary said, "I think in due time you'll see this will be done. I don't think we'll be in the first tranche at all though."
The first batch of cabinet choices Clinton is expected to name is his national security team including secretaries of state and defense.
On whether she recommended a name to the White House, O'Leary said, "I'm not discussing that with anyone in the press."

In talks with White House officials on her replacement, O'Leary said she has discussed "how important it is to have a person who understands the task of managing large, complex technical organizations, and someone who also understands in that task the necessity to continue to drive for stripping out redundent functions, reducing costs...while delivering on the extraordinary missions."
Those rumored to be under consideration for the energy secretary post include current Deputy Energy Secretary Charles Curtis and Democratic Rep. Bill Richardson of New Mexico.
